metas.name: Argentina - Roadlines
metas.note: • Road lines in Argentina are mainly dashed white, double yellow or a mix in between.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Australia - Full White
metas.note: • Australia uses almost exclusively white road lines, with a few rare exceptions in alpine regions such as Mount Kosciuszko and Mount Hotham.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Canada - Single Yellow
metas.note:
• Canadian roads usually have single yellow centre lines.
  • However, double middle yellow centre lines are still decently common.

--- NOTE:

  • Double yellow centre lines are more common in the US.
  • This is not a 100% reliable clue, so make sure to use this along with other clues.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Chile - Full White & Yellow
metas.note: • Chilean road lines are either all white, or all yellow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Denmark - Small Squares
metas.note:
• Outer road lines often consist of small white squares.
  • These unique-looking lines are a good way to identify Denmark.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/denmark.

metas.name: Estonia - Short Dashed Outers
metas.note:
• Outer road lines sometimes consist of short dashes.

--- NOTE:

  • Lithuania also sometimes has short dashes.
  • In addition, Sweden primarily uses short dashes as outer road lines.
  • Sweden's dashes are closer the edge.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/estonia.

metas.name: Finland - Full Outers
metas.note:
• Where present, outer road lines will always be solid white lines.

--- NOTE:

  • Unlike Sweden and Norway, Finland does not use dashed outside lines.

--- TIP:

  • Norway (Normal)
  • Sweden (Short)
  • Finland (Full)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/finland.

metas.name: France - Offset Blocks
metas.note:
• These middle road lines, where each dash consists of two offset blocks, are unique to France.
  • They are not extremely common, but when you see them, you can safely guess France.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/france.

metas.name: Greece - Double Faded
metas.note:
• In Greece you will commonly see slightly faded, solid white double middle lines.
  • This can be used to distinguish it from most other Mediterranean countries.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/greece.

metas.name: Ireland - Yellow Dashed Outers
metas.note:
• It is very common to see yellow outside dashes on Irish roads.

--- NOTE:

  • This is essentially never found in the UK.
  • These dashes can also be seen in New Zealand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/ireland.

metas.name: Israel - Yellow Outers
metas.note:
• Most roads feature yellow outer lines with white centre lines.

--- NOTE:

These roadlines also exist in:

  • Jordan
  • Qatar
  • UAE
  • Oman
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank.

metas.name: Malaysia - Double White
metas.note:
• Malaysia frequently uses double white centre lines on its two-lane roads.
  • It is the only Southeast Asian country to do so.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Mexico - Single Yellow
metas.note:
• The most typical Mexican road lines are white solid outer lines with a single unbroken yellow middle line.

--- NOTE:

  • Single broken yellow middle lines and double yellow middle lines are also common.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: New Zealand - Roadlines
metas.note:
• New Zealand normally uses white outer road lines.
  • Yellow dashed outer road lines can be seen in populated areas.
  • Roads with no outer lines can be seen on smaller roads.
  • Inner lines are either a single dashed white line or unbroken double yellow lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Norway - Long Dashed Outers
metas.note:
• Smaller Norwegian roads typically have long dashed white outer lines, while larger roads have solid outer lines and yellow middle lines.
  • The yellow lines have a distinct tinge of orange.

--- TIP:

  • Norway (Normal)
  • Sweden (Short)
  • Finland (Full)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Philippines - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Middle road lines in the Philippines can be either yellow or white.
  • In particular, you will often see combined yellow and white middle lines, which is not common in any other East Asian country.
  • Yellow road lines commonly have a distinct orange tint.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/philippines.

metas.name: Poland - Double White
metas.note:
• Poland has all-white road lines.
  • Double middle lines are very common and usually a good clue for Poland.

--- NOTE:

  • Some other European countries, most notably Denmark and Greece, can have double middle lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/poland.

metas.name: Senegal - White Dashed Outers
metas.note: • Being a former French colony, Senegal uses French infrastructure such as bollards, poles, signs and road lines.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/senegal.

metas.name: South Africa - Tripples
metas.note:
• South Africa occasionally features unique white triple centre lines.

--- NOTE:

  • The only other countries where you will find road lines like these are the other southern African countries of Botswana, Eswatini, and Lesotho.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: South Africa - Yellow Outers
metas.note:
• On most roads, South Africa utilizes single yellow outer lines and white centre lines.

--- NOTE:

These roadlines also exist in:

  • Botswana
  • Eswatini
  • Lesotho
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: Sweden - Short Dashed Outers
metas.note:
• On smaller roads, the outer road lines are white and dashed.
  • In contrast to Norway and Finland, all road lines are white.

--- TIP:

  • Norway (Normal)
  • Sweden (Short)
  • Finland (Full)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: United States - Double Yellow
metas.note:
• The US uses yellow middle lines and white outer lines.
  • Double middle lines are the most common.

--- NOTE:

  • Double middle lines are less common in Canada, but not rare – use this meta with caution.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: United States - Rumble Strips
metas.note:
• Interstate highways, US highways, and some state roads have rumble strips in each edge of the road.
  • These are small indentations in the pavement perpendicular to the road.
  • They can be located on the outside edges of the road and in between lanes on multi-lane highways.

--- NOTE:

  • Rumble strips may appear in Canada or Mexico, but are much more rare.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: Uruguay - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Uruguay often has these triple road lines, that consist of double yellow roadlines with white dashes in between.
  • This is a design not seen anywhere else in the Americas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.
